newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian minister opposes further Belgacom sale.
newsitem.headline: Belgian minister opposes further Belgacom sale.

text.p: Belgian Telecommunications Minister Elio Di Rupo opposes any further privatisation of state-held telephone company Belgacom, his spokesman said on Tuesday.
"As long as Di Rupo is Telecommunications minister, Belgacom will stay majority public (held)," Marc Janssen told Reuters.

He was commenting on newspaper reports on Tuesday that Belgacom management urged the Belgian state to sell its 50.1 stake in the operator and alleviate its hefty pension charges by injecting the capital gain on the sale in its Pension Fund.
"Some may have a different opinion but he is the minister who is responsible for the company and he has always said he'll oppose any widening of the privatisation," Janssen said.
"This is a proposal of management but I don't see what could make him change his mind," he added.
The rest of Belgacom's capital -- 49.9 percent -- is owned by a consortium including Ameritech, Singapore Telecom, TeleDanmark and three Belgian investors.
The Wall Street Journal Europe said that senior management were urging the Belgian government to sell its stake through an initial public offering in excess of $2 billion.
Belgacom was not available for comment.
